title: Machine learning guides discovery of selective submicromolar CK2 inhibitors
summary: The accepted-paper abstract reports that docking, CDK-liability filtering, machine learning and error prediction guided more selective CK2 inhibitor leads. The authors report submicromolar hits and a 90% pipeline hit rate; kinase-assay figures support biochemical inhibition. These are discovery-stage compounds, with no demonstrated clinical benefit. The hit rate describes the authors' selected pipeline, not a general drug-discovery success rate.
ai_technology: Machine learning; prediction-error modeling; molecular docking
organization: University of Helsinki; Chemotargets; University of Girona; University of Turku; Åbo Akademi University

evidence.tested: Kinase-assay figures report CK2 inhibition by selected hit compounds.
evidence.unknown: Full study methods, independent reproduction and clinical outcomes were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: ML and error prediction prioritized compounds after docking and off-target filtering.
